correctness.rationale: An isolated designated chord forces independent uniform matchings on its complementary even arcs. The conditional crossing expectation differs from the unconditional expectation by -(ab+n-1)/3. Rotation-counting the possible chords yields the exact negative covariance formula; the geometric q-ratio gives the three-term expansion and the distinct persistent -1/3 rare contribution. An explicit second-moment bound shows I-S converges to zero in L2, while Var(S) tends to one and the classical exact Var(C) yields the correlation limit. The standard-library checker passed 1304 finite exact assertions including 135135 complete diagrams at n=7; finite checks do not replace infinite arguments.

originality.rationale: The primary distinct assertion is the exact all-isolated-chord/crossing covariance and the persistent limiting covariance -1/3 of the non-simple isolated correction, despite that correction vanishing in L2. A prior exact joint enumerator for simple chords and crossings already gives the simple-chord dependence and the leading correlation constant; those are excluded as novel. The inspected primary literature gives crossing and component marginals, degree laws, or separate simple-chord bounds, not this mixed all-isolated correction. A general joint enumerator may nevertheless encode it implicitly.
residual_risks: A more general historic multivariate chord-diagram generating function may implicitly yield the all-isolated mixed moment and is not exhaustively excluded.
A prior simple-chord mixed enumerator covers the leading covariance and leading correlation constant; these are not distinct original contributions.
The originality conclusion is best-knowledge review against inspected sources, not independent priority certification.

value.rationale: Isolated vertices in the random chord-intersection graph and its total edge count are canonical statistics. A finite-order structural distinction matters: non-simple isolated chords vanish in L2, yet their covariance with crossings converges to -1/3, so deleting them incorrectly changes the constant-order correction. The exact all-dimensional sign, arc factorization and sharp finite-size expansion provide a meaningful dependence law rather than a routine rephrasing of the known simple-chord count.
